subject.title: [Bug]: Schema-version error blames a downgrade that never happened; version string cannot identify the stale build

question: Should this issue be scoped to actionable stale-build diagnostics only, while keeping `doctor --fix` blocked from opening a database whose schema is newer than the executing build supports?
rationale: The reporter’s recovery problem is valid, but allowing doctor to cross the schema ceiling would change the established state-safety boundary and cannot be inferred safely from diagnostics alone.

options.title: Improve diagnostics; keep the gate
options.body: Add build/install and schema-version detail to the error, while continuing to refuse newer databases before doctor performs any repair.

options.title: Design a separate guarded recovery mode
options.body: Only pursue a new migration/recovery mode after defining its data-safety contract, supported operations, and proof that it cannot mutate unsupported newer state.

recommendation.title: Improve diagnostics; keep the gate
recommendation.body: Add build/install and schema-version detail to the error, while continuing to refuse newer databases before doctor performs any repair.

likelyOwner.reason: The related merged work owns the current schema-version safety boundary and is the clearest history-based routing point.
